title: ASP.NET Core CORS antiforgery rate limiting HTTPS and security headers
concepts: CORS is a browser-enforced cross-origin response-sharing protocol, not authentication or authorization. The server's policy tells browsers which origins, methods, and headers may participate; non-browser clients are not constrained by CORS.

Antiforgery protects browser-originated state-changing requests that carry ambient credentials. ASP.NET Core 11 adds automatic Fetch Metadata/Origin checks for form-processing endpoints; the classic request-token and protected-cookie pair remains available and can coexist.

Rate limiting constrains resource consumption using request-count windows or concurrency bounds. Choose partition keys that reflect the abuse and workload model, bound queues, and treat in-process limits as per-instance unless a distributed coordination design is added.

HTTPS redirection and HSTS solve different jobs: redirection moves an HTTP request to HTTPS, while HSTS teaches a browser to use HTTPS for future requests. Reverse proxies may already perform these functions, so forwarded scheme trust and deployment topology determine where the policies belong.

Security headers add browser protections such as content-type sniffing and framing restrictions. ASP.NET Core does not provide a universal CSP authoring policy; header values must match the app's resource model and be tested before enforcement.

inventory.title: HTTPS redirection, HSTS, proxy termination, and browser response security headers
items: Avoid duplicate proxy and app HTTPS redirects
Security header does not replace output encoding

Use ASP.NET Core 11 reference docs for middleware and option APIs. Rate-limiter algorithms and CORS/antiforgery concepts are stable across recent major releases; no artificial per-version lesson is needed.

In current ASP.NET Core, registering antiforgery services with AddAntiforgery does not itself add middleware. Blazor and Minimal API request processing must explicitly include UseAntiforgery where required; MVC and Razor Pages use their antiforgery filters.
Reverse proxy deployments can terminate TLS and emit HSTS or redirects. Configure the app and proxy as one system, and trust forwarded scheme headers only from known proxies.

ASP.NET Core 11 adds default automatic CSRF protection in WebApplication.CreateBuilder apps. It uses Sec-Fetch-Site and Origin metadata, records a verdict, and relies on form-processing components to enforce denied results; the classic paired-token system remains available and can coexist.

WithOrigins values must not contain a trailing slash. CORS simple requests and credentials follow current Fetch safelist and credentials-mode rules, with cookie SameSite/privacy policy as an independent constraint.

For endpoint-specific rate policies, UseRateLimiter follows UseRouting and must see authentication before a user-key partition. A global-only limiter can precede routing. Built-in state is per instance.
HSTS defaults to 30 days, no subdomains, and no preload. HTTPS redirection defaults to 307; distinguish HTTPS_PORT redirect configuration from HTTPS_PORTS listener configuration.
